- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event balance is heavily bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often underestimates drop; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often overestimates price; apply 1–3% downward correction to forecast mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0) and price is trending up, model may lag; add 1–3% lag correction to forecast to align with sentiment.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 15-day MA unless sentiment strongly contradicts.  
- When multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast slope by 5–10% for next 10–15 days to account for event saturation.
